How we work

Each agent tells you what it did, not what it can do.

Two more jobs, in the agents' own words. Four more live at the cases page.

Comparing notes on the sidewalk, phone in hand.

Arthur
Commercial real estate, Raleigh-Durham

I only bring you the ones worth a look.

Every morning I go through the listing and market-data platforms your team already subscribes to and check new multifamily listings against the buy box: 100-plus units, 1980s or newer, value-add. Most weeks that's forty or fifty new listings. I bring you three or four.

4 of 51 listings matched the buy box this week

I draft the note. I don't send it until you say go. Arthur, on file

Storm season doesn't wait for the office to open.

Wade
Storm response, roofing

I turn a hail map into a street list before lunch.

When a storm swath posts for the service area, I work out which streets are actually worth a knock: hail size, roof age, a crew that isn't already booked two streets over. Then I rank the list so nobody gets knocked twice. Anyone who says “call me later” stays on a list I follow up on my own, because that's usually where the job was going to get lost.

11 inspections recovered off the follow-up list last month

I never knock on a door that hasn't already opened one to us. Wade, on file

You never have to log in

The portal is real.You just won't need it much.

Every agent keeps a work log, a list of connected tools, and settings you can change any time. Most weeks, the work just arrives and you never open the tab.

  • A real portal. Work log, tools, settings. Open it whenever you want to.
  • Permanent memory. Tell it once. It doesn't ask again.
  • A ceiling you set. It asks before it goes over.

Your logins. Your tools.

It works inside the accountsyou already pay for.

Every agent connects to your accounts the way your bank asks you to log in through a browser: encrypted, and revocable the moment you want it gone. We never ask for a password we don't need.

There are always a couple of platforms nobody formally integrates with: the listing and market-data sites your team already has a login for. An agent can work inside those directly, the same way you would: reading the screen, clicking the same buttons, under your own account.

Gmail Calendar Sheets Drive QuickBooks Xero Stripe HubSpot Notion Calendly Airtable Asana Trello Dropbox Zapier Zoom Shopify

What we won't do

  • Contact your customers without you asking first.
  • Send anything before you've approved it, until you tell us otherwise.
  • Touch a tool you haven't connected. Your logins, not ours.

What this costs

What a coordinator costs, and what this costs.

A full-time coordinator runs $55,000 a year before benefits, before the desk, before the laptop. Every tier here still comes in under that, and the agent's on the clock before your coffee's cold.

Each agent has its own inbox and its own memory. Your first agent is your plan's price, and each one you add after that is 20% off. Nobody on your team pays to read its work. You're hiring, not licensing seats.

The build is billed once, at the start, not every month. It's a flat $5,000 on Growth and Scale. On Starter it's $1,000 to $2,500, quoted once we know the job. Count it into the first year and every tier still comes in under a coordinator.
